title: Set two carts out for an automated refuse truck: lids to the street, 3 ft clear
instruction: Set both wheeled carts out for the automated refuse truck. Stand each cart on the verge with its lid opening toward the street (the white arrow, square to the kerb within 25 degrees; handle and wheels toward the house), its front 0 to 30 mm (0 to 0.3 m at this 1:10 scale) behind the kerb and not on it. Keep each cart at least 91 mm (3 feet) from the other cart, the mailbox and its post, the hydrant and the parked car, and off the driveway.
context: Refuse and recyclable material collectors drive automated side-loader trucks: an arm reaches out from the truck, grabs each wheeled cart, lifts it and tips it into the hopper. The arm can only grab a cart that stands at the kerb with its lid opening toward the street (handle and wheels toward the house) and with about 3 feet (0.9 m) of space around it: from the next cart, mailboxes, poles, hydrants and parked cars. Cities and haulers print this rule on collection calendars and mould an arrow into the lids that points to the street. A cart set out wrongly is skipped, or the driver steps down and re-sets it by hand; walk-up services for residents who cannot move their own carts set them out the same way. This hauler wants carts on the verge, never on the kerb or in the road, where they block traffic. Here a 1:10 street stands on the table, and both carts must be set out for one pass of the truck.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the verge (the strip of pavement between the house and the street) of a residential street at 1:10 scale; the house is behind the arm bases. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases (toward the street), y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Fixed: (1) Kerb: a light grey concrete block 10 mm wide (x 39.0 to 40.0 cm) and 12 mm tall, from y -64.0 to y +36.0 cm; its face toward the arms (x 39.0 cm) is the kerb line. (2) Road: a dark grey asphalt sheet 1 mm thick, x 40.0 to 60.0 cm, y -64.0 to +64.0 cm. (3) Driveway: a pale concrete sheet 1 mm thick crossing the verge to the road, x 24.0 to 40.0 cm, y +36.0 to +64.0 cm (the kerb is dropped there). (4) Mailbox: a galvanised steel post (a cylinder 16 mm across and 105 mm tall) centred at x 37.0 cm, y 0, carrying a black painted steel mailbox, a box 40 mm long (x 35.0 to 39.0 cm), 16 mm wide and 20 mm tall (105 to 125 mm up). (5) Fire hydrant: a red painted cast-iron cylinder 24 mm across and 55 mm tall with a bonnet (a red painted cast-iron cylinder 18 mm across and 10 mm tall) on top, centred at x 36.5 cm, y +30.0 cm. (6) Parked car: a dark blue painted wooden block 180 mm in x (41.0 to 59.0 cm), 340 mm along the kerb in y (-64.0 to -30.0 cm) and 80 mm tall, standing on the road 10 mm off the kerb, with a grey-blue painted wooden cabin block 160 x 200 x 60 mm on top (x 42.0 to 58.0 cm, y -57.0 to -37.0 cm). Loose: (7) Two wheeled refuse carts, 1:10 models of an empty 240-litre automated-collection cart, each one rigid 120 g body of dark grey HDPE with no moving parts: a body 73 mm front to back, 58 mm across and 95 mm tall; a lid of the same 73 x 58 mm, 6 mm thick, on top (top 101 mm up), green on one cart and blue on the other; at the back, standing 6 mm proud of the body, a black handle bar 58 mm across and 10 mm tall (85 to 95 mm up) and two black wheels 16 mm wide and 24 mm tall at the bottom corners; and a white arrow 1 mm thick on the lid, 39 mm long and up to 20 mm wide, pointing to the front (the side the lid opens on). Footprint: 79 mm front to back (handle and wheels included) and 58 mm across. Start: near the house, side-on, fronts toward each other, 187 mm apart: the green-lidded cart with the centre of its body at x 22.0 cm, y +13.0 cm, its front toward -y (the midline); the blue-lidded cart at x 22.0 cm, y -13.0 cm, its front toward +y. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the carts' poses at the last step, as a top photo with a tape and a protractor would read it. A cart's footprint is its 79 x 58 mm outline seen from above (handle and wheels included; for a tilted cart, the shadow of its whole box); its front is the lid's opening side, where the white arrow points. Standing: tilted 10 degrees or less, its lowest point within 3 mm of the verge, and still (the centre of its base moved under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s, turns counted at its corners). Facing the street: its front within 25 degrees of +x (square to the kerb, toward the road). At the kerb: the footprint's most forward point 0 to 30 mm behind the kerb face (x 36.0 to 39.0 cm; up to 2 mm past it allowed for contact). On the driveway: any part of the footprint over the driveway sheet. Clear: the footprint at least 91 mm (3 ft at scale) seen from above from the other cart's footprint, the mailbox and its post (the mailbox's 40 x 16 mm outline covers the post), the hydrant's 24 mm circle and the car's 180 x 340 mm outline. The trial scores 0 if either cart is knocked over (tilted more than 45 degrees) or any part of either cart's footprint is more than 2 mm past the kerb face's line (on the kerb, in the road, or past the line where it crosses the driveway). Otherwise each cart earns 0.5 if it is standing, off the driveway, facing the street, at the kerb and clear; 0.25 if it is all of those but not clear (within 91 mm of the other cart, the mailbox, the hydrant or the car); else 0 (left at the house, side-on or with its handle to the street, more than 30 mm back, on the driveway, lifted, moving or leaning). The score is the sum of the two: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0, and the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Either cart may go on either side. For a cart square to the kerb with its front 12 mm behind it, the only clear places are with the centre of its body at y +12.8 to +16.8 cm (between the mailbox and the hydrant) or y -18.6 to -12.8 cm (between the mailbox and the car); each holds one cart. Examples: the start 0; one cart set out between the mailbox and the hydrant, the other left at the house, 0.5; both set out, one within 91 mm of the mailbox, 0.75; both clear 1.0; both at the kerb in the stretch left of the mailbox (too close to each other) 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5; a cart with its handle to the street 0 for that cart; a cart in the road 0 for the trial. In a real trial: a tape square to the kerb for the set-back, a tape between outlines for the clearances, a protractor on the lid arrow for the facing.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The kerb, street furniture and car are fixed. Each cart is one rigid, empty body of nine boxes: its wheels do not roll and its lid does not open, so it is lifted and carried rather than tipped back and wheeled, and the truck is not simulated. The scorer sees only the carts, so a cart held still within 3 mm of the verge counts as standing. 3 ft is 91 mm at 1:10.
reset_notes: Stand the green-lidded cart with the centre of its body at x 22.0 cm, y +13.0 cm, its front toward -y, and the blue-lidded cart at x 22.0 cm, y -13.0 cm, its front toward +y (fronts toward each other, 187 mm apart), both standing upright on their bases and wheels. Everything else is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
